But before you do so, Ms. Hanson, if you need any -- if you need to consult any material, please, address the Court, and we allowed you to fetch some material apparently you were seeking. I also understood that you wanted to consult the 19th of December instructions, which have been printed out for you from the 65 ter version and are available if you want to look at them.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. That was the item I wished to fetch, but since I was told it could be made available here, I didn't go to my office. I just wanted to review it. I hadn't looked at it in a while. That's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I hope that you have the instruction with you now. If you don't, then it is with pleasure, Your Honours, for practical purposes to provide a copy to our present-day witness. I think that we'll move faster that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, if you have printed out a copy that could be provided to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I understood that a copy was provided by VWS already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I left it in the witness room, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you need it tell us. Otherwise, another one will be printed --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, it's here on the -- it's on the screen. It's okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed. I see the Defence --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: If you wish to give it to me, that would be handy. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's -- Mr. Usher, could you assist? Or Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. I'm providing the English version so I don't think we should be having a problem with that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We leave it to the witness if she wants to consult the original language. Then we could perhaps do that on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It's fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, we were discussing paragraph 21 of your report and your conclusion that, according to Variant A, the laws of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina were no longer to be abided by and that orders of parallel Serb authorities were to be followed. Then I asked you something else.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, again, I will be using the instructions now on the organisation and activity of the Serb people in Bosnia-Herzegovina according to 65 ter. That is 28 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you are really speaking too fast.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do apologise. Instructions on the activity of the Serb people in BH, 65 ter 28386. And now I would like to ask you that we focus on the last page, section 3, paragraph 2, both in B/C/S and in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what is stated in that paragraph: "In their work and activity, the organs of authority are obliged to act in keeping with the federal constitution and federal laws and other federal regulations, as well as the republican regulations which are not contrary to the federal regulations." Do you see that, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Will you agree with me that, according to this kind of interpretation of the text of the instructions, the regulations of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina are not being annulled except for those that are in contravention of federal regulations; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is instructing the Bosnian Serbs to choose to ignore some republican regulations.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If a republican regulation is contrary to a federal regulation, will you agree with me that it is the federal regulation that has supremacy?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you on that issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware of a single regulation - so if we're talking about December 1991 - that was at that time in contravention of a federal regulation? And I'm asking you all of this because you, in paragraph 21, as you analyse this instruction, said that laws of the SRBiH laws were to stop being abided by.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not aware of such a regulation, and such a regulation would be presumably resolved at the level of the constitutional court which is why I find it curious that so many SDS organs are constantly repeating that refrain of not obeying any republic regulation that is not in accordance with federal. Given that we don't expect all these people named to be members of the Crisis Staffs to be constitutional experts themselves, it gives, I find, a certain leeway in interpretation. But I also -- I'm referring to the instructions in a totality, such as setting up parallel organs, taking over police stations, things like that, that are presumably not in accordance with republican law.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is It precisely this theory of the takeover of police stations that led you to say this in paragraph 21; namely that, according to Variant A, Crisis Staffs were to stop abiding by SRBiH laws and follow the orders of parallel Serb authorities? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I say, it's the total effect of these instructions. It's the instruction on police stations, and it's item 2 in the last section, on which I base that conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to go back to that preamble now and ask you the following. Was it possible for someone at local level to reach a decision to refuse call-up and to refuse to act in accordance with the obligation of answering call-up that is based on federal law?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course, it was possible. Many people avoided call-up or refused it. Whether -- if you're asking if it's possible. Yes, it is possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Would that have been legal?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Will you say that I'm right if I say that precisely in the period that you analyse, that is to say, the second half of 1991 and 1992, the Serb population -- or rather, the non-Serb population did not respond to call-up?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's pretty far out of the ambit of my tasking as looking at Crisis Staffs, but I'm certainly aware of that in general terms, yes. It's not something that I've looked at specifically for this report, but I'm aware of that in general.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Then I won't be dealing with this any longer, but thank you for your assistance. Now I'd like to draw your attention to a part of your analysis that has to do with the structure of Crisis Staffs. You'll be needing that document. In paragraph 24, P379 - I'm saying that for the sake of the transcript, that is your report - this is what you say. Could you please follow what I'm reading, Ms. Hanson. "According to that document" - you're actually referring to the instruction - "the Crisis Staff was headed by the president of the SDS Municipal Board, who in most Serb-majority municipalities was also the president of the municipal assembly." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Now, again, I'd like to ask for the following. For the transcript I'm saying this. This is 65 ter 28386. It's a Prosecution document. It is the instruction on the organisation and activity of organs dated the 19th of December. So could we please have a look at this together. It's in e-court as well. Let us look at the first chapter, Variant A, paragraph 3. It's the third page in B/C/S, and I think it's the third page in English too. So it is paragraph 3. We'll wait for a second now. Thank you. This is what it says there. In paragraph 3, the members of the Crisis Staff are referred to in terms of the office they hold. And then it says: "The commander of the Crisis Staff is the president of the municipal assembly or the chairman of the municipal -- the -- the Municipal Board." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: This is what I'm asking you now. As for the Crisis Staffs for which you had access to their documents, the president of the assembly, or the president of the Executive Council, was it, at the same time, the president of the SDS?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not in every municipality, no. It was a general pattern, but not in every municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So will we agree that, according to these instructions, the commander of the Crisis Staff is someone who holds two of the possible offices, either the president of the -- either the president of the assembly or the president of the Executive Board, not the president of the SDS; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct for Variant A. However, in Variant A municipalities, it was generally the pattern that the president of the Municipal Board of the SDS was president of the assembly. It is not everywhere. And I'm sure it's -- this -- orders are only for the Serb people. So if it should be a municipality where the president of the municipal assembly is not a Serb, he was not going to enter the Crisis Staff. He was not going to be commander of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: No, my question is a simple one, and now I'm talking about Variant A. Do we agree that, according to the instruction, the commander of the Crisis Staff does not necessarily have to be the president of the SDS. But he has to be either the president of the assembly or the president of the Executive Board of the local community?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, according to the instruction, that's how it reads.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And then we're going back to paragraph 24 of your report, would it be correct to say what you wrote here? Namely, that, according to this document, the Crisis Staff was headed by the president of the SDS Municipal Board?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was trying to combine the general effect of Variant A and Variant B together to give the general pattern. But, no, it would not be correctly exactly as written in paragraph 24 because there could be cases in which the president of the SDS Municipal Board was not the president of the municipal assembly in a Serb-majority municipality and therefore he would not be, according to this instruction, the commander of the Crisis Staff. But there was always some local variations, depending on personalities and other things. I'm trying to describe a general pattern, and I -- as written in the sentence, yeah, the clauses should be shifted around.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I dealt with this for a long time. That's why I wanted to ask you this. This perplexed me. Look at the instruction now.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is 28386.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And this is what I'd like to focus your attention on. Chapter 2, Variant B, paragraph 3. This is what it says there in Variant B, and that is the establishment of Crisis Staffs in the municipality where the Serb population is a minority. Namely, the commander of the Crisis Staff is the president of the Municipal Board of the SDS. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So the situation is an interesting one there. In Variant A, the commander of the Crisis Staff is the president of the municipality or the president of the Executive Board; but in Variant B, that is to say, where the Serb population is a minority in the local community, it is imperative that the commander of the Crisis Staff has to be the president of the SDS. Did you notice that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It doesn't say "imperative" but it gives the instructions. Yes, I see the distinction, and I agree. In my sentence I may have -- I conflated the two separate instructions. But, once again, in a Variant A, he was going -- the president of the municipality would almost invariably be if not the president of the SDS, a high -- a member of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That is quite different now but I wanted us to clarify this in respect of what you had said. However, I'd like to ask you the following. If you observed this difference in terms of the person who is the commander of the Crisis Staff in Variant A and Variant B, as you dealt with your research, were you in a position to draw a conclusion as to why the author did something like that, like why did he in Variant B give greater power to the president of the SDS in Variant B rather than in Variant A where the local community has a majority Serb population?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a Variant B municipality, the SDS did not hold all the municipal leadership positions. So therefore, the positions on -- corresponding positions on the Crisis Staff are going to go to the SDS candidates for those positions. In most municipalities, not all, but in most, the SDS candidate for the position of municipal assembly president would be the president of the SDS Municipal Board. Therefore, I see them as parallel structures the -- between Variant A and B there is considerable parallels and I don't see Variant A as lessening the power of the SDS because it's clear that the Crisis Staff is to be formed within the SDS with the leadership of the SDS Municipal Board. So I don't see that Variant B is giving more power to the SDS than Variant A. I don't see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I put it to you that in 1991, in all municipalities and in all local communities, there was a coalition between the ruling or among the ruling nationalist -- national parties and that there was a certain key according to which functions were distributed. And that in all the municipalities that you studied, i.e., Sanski Most, Prijedor, Kljuc, Bijeljina, Zvornik, Foca, Rajlovac, East Sarajevo, the power was distributed among national parties, SDA, SDS, and HDZ. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. There was the national key and functions were distributed among the national -- the winning parties which were generally the national parties. Not in Rajlovac because that wasn't created until February 1992 and it was a creation of the SDS so there were no non-SDS people appointed, as far as I know. But in the others, yes, the national key was followed. Who won the most -- whichever party won the most in the local elections got president of the municipal assembly or president of the Executive Board. It was agreed. And yes, power was shared after the 1990 elections.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you mean to say that you reached such a conclusion through your analysis? But who within the system elected the commander of the Crisis Staff, or was he appointed by the republican grassroots?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, your question doesn't make sense as translated. "Appointed by the republican grassroots" doesn't make sense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you please rephrase your question, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand. I'll take it step by step.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Ms. Hanson, based on your analysis, who was it who elected the president or commander of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to this, he is not elected. He is named by these instructions.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: That is precisely why I formulated my question as I did. If both the president of the assembly and president of the Executive Board are Serbs - I will assume that an SDS president will be a Serb - who will be chosen to be the commander of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I would have to look at those municipalities where both those positions were held by Serbs and then look at the Crisis Staffs. I can't say off the top of my head the instructions don't explicate.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. While we are still within the e-court system on this 65 ter document, 28386, let us look at chapter 1, Variant A, item 11. Sub-item 2. If I may, Ms. Hanson, I'll read it out. We're referring to the first degree of Variant A, the functioning of the Crisis Staff, which reads, item 11, make preparations for, and I quote: "... the replenishment of war units according to JNA specifications both with personnel and materiel, equipment, and livestock from the mobilisation fund in keeping with federal regulations and on the basis of the Serbian people's principles of justice and humanity, which includes SDS officials and other leaders and people of standing among the Serbian people serving as personal examples." My question: This provision concerning the replenishment of war units, which is in keeping with the federal regulations, is it something that you find controversial in any way or is that an obligation that had previously been laid down?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it would be a pre-existing obligation, so it is not controversial, as far as I can see. Although it is clearly heading towards the Serbianisation of the JNA units in that it's encouraging Serbs to sign up and it's not saying anything about encouraging the rest of the population. But by itself, it's the obligation, as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask this again. You mentioned, or at least I heard it in interpretation, "Serbianisation of the JNA." Does it state anywhere here in the first degree of Variant A that it applied to the Serb people only? Or -- or let me stop here.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: These instructions are clearly aimed at the Serb people only. But, no, here -- in the reference to the JNA, it doesn't specify Serbs only. But the instructions are for Serbs only.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: And would you find anything controversial in a person responding to a legally determined obligation? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, just for my understanding, you made a quote from paragraph 11, and you asked the witness whether it's controversial or not. Do I then understand that it is your interpretation of paragraph 11 that to apply federal regulations and Serbian people's principles of justice and humanity rather than all people's principles of justice and humanity is not controversial. Is that what I have to understand is the position of the Defence? I mean, in paragraph 11, we have a reference to the principles of justice and humanity of the Serbian people alone and not of any of the other peoples. And therefore I'm wondering whether I fully understood your questions or whether I fully understood what you wished to elicit as evidence from this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, Your Honour, there is no justice or humanity that would belong to one people only. It is a universal principle. This was a time in December. And that is why a call was issued by the SDS and it addressed, above all, the SDS members.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now, you said above all SDS members. Did it address anyone else than SDS members? I mean, I'm asking for the position of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence continues to maintain that a general mobilisation call was a general call and was a duty, an obligation established under law for all citizens of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Or when you when refer to "and that is why a call was issued by the SDS," I understood that to be a reference to these instructions. Now, in your answer, whether anyone else was addressed apart from SDS members, you were referring to a mobilisation call, which confuses me a bit, but if that is your answer, then I'll invite you to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Perhaps, in a way, it anticipated my next question. We're staying with the same document; 65 ter 28386, the instructions. Let us now direct our attention to step 2 of Variant A, item 2, where matters are placed a bit differently, especially in light of Their Honours' question.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It reads here that at the second stage of Variant A, it is necessary to, as it reads: "Mobilise all police forces from among the Serbian people, and in co-operation with the JNA commands and staffs, gradually resubordinate them." This is what I'm interested in. In the first step or stage of Variant A, there was a call to mobilise people from among the Serbian people, so did you analyse the difference in the status between the first and second step, or stage, of Variant A?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I say that, first -- the first degree is the preparations, and the second degree is the actual assumption of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In the process of takeover of power, according to these instructions, the police forces from the ranks of the Serb people are to be mobilised. Is that the correct conclusion?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says here, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain for us now what do you mean by this: "In co-operation with JNA commands and staffs, gradually resubordinate them." Who is supposed to be resubordinated to whom, according to these instructions?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The police forces, as I read it, are to be resubordinated to the JNA commands and staffs.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Bearing in mind the fact that the time is December 1991, I'd like to know, up until April of 1992, did your analysis arrive at instances where the police forces were resubordinated in this period before the outbreak of hostilities in Bosnia-Herzegovina by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The second stage wasn't activated until the 14th of February, 1992. But I did not look at police forces and their resubordination to the JNA. I simply didn't look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The fact that you didn't analyse it, would that mean that you don't know whether at any point before April of 1992 there were any police forces resubordinated by the JNA?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we look at your report again. For the transcript, it's P379. And we will focus on paragraph 69 where you say --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Where it says the military role of the Crisis Staffs - that's chapter 69 - you say: "The common denominator everywhere is co-ordination and support by the Crisis Staff. The further end of the spectrum is the Crisis Staff giving operational orders to armed units, and the head of the Crisis Staff personally commanding armed units." This is what I'd like to ask you about first. What sort of function is that, head or chief of the Crisis Staff? Who do you consider to be the head of the Crisis Staff who can personally issue orders to armed units?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was called either the president or, in some cases, the commander of the Crisis Staff. That's who I refer to.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: So I'd be right in saying that, to you, the head of the Crisis Staff is, according to the instructions, the commander of the Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: The instructions of 19 December used the term "commander." I more often see the term "president of the Crisis Staff" in the documents themselves, but I do occasionally see the term "commander." But when I said the head of the Crisis Staff, translated here as "nacelnik," I meant the president or commander, whatever he calls himself.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: In your analysis of numerous documents seized from Crisis Staffs, did you find the term "head of Crisis Staff" anywhere?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I'm sorry if the translation gave the term "nacelnik" which has, I realise, a more specific meaning in B/C/S. I may just have been tired of writing "president" or "commander." I do not mean to say any -- I never saw the term "nacelnik" and I don't mean to say that there was -- I think I just didn't want to type out "president." Do you understand? I'm not asserting there is such a position as "nacelnik" at all. I mean "president" or "commander."

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Now we know who we are talking about. Let me ask you this: Bearing in mind the time when the Army of Republika Srpska was established, the 21st of May, 1992, the adoption of the Law on the Army, was it in legal terms at all possible for someone, be he commander or president of the Crisis Staff, to issue operational orders to the Army of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said, I'm not a lawyer and I have not studied the Law on the Army precisely. But these -- all these institutions were forming -- in the process of formation and there was a great deal of improvisation going on and the different groups and organs were writing their own rules often enough. Legally, I don't know. I imagine not. What I see on the ground is another matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me now put a question which supports my own statement. And I put it to you that it is impossible in a system of singleness of command and subordination for someone who is a president or commander of the Crisis Staff to issue orders to the army. In view of the numerous documents that have passed through your hands, would you agree with me that in terms of regulations, as they exist, it would be impossible?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: There's what is allowed and not allowed and there's what's possible or impossible, I'm sorry, but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to keep matters clear. Have you a formed an opinion, on the basis of your expertise, on whether a president or commander of the Crisis Staff was formally empowered to issue orders to the army? On the basis of the regulations, the existing law, whatever, have you formed an opinion about that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I have not examined the laws in such detail that I could form a really informed opinion, but generally, my impression would be no, he could not do it to the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now the next question is, because you made a clear distinction between what you saw in the -- what the formal position was and what happened on the ground, have you seen documents in which presidents or commanders of the Crisis Staff issued orders to military persons or units?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Operational orders.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you say your impression, not more than that, not an expert opinion about what would not be legal on paper, does not match with what you saw in the documents you examined, to the extent that it nevertheless happened on the ground, at least on paper again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's quite correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, please proceed. When I say "please proceed," perhaps it's better to say let's take a break. We'll take a break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00. Could the witness first be escorted out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And could I inquire with you, Mr. Stojanovic, how much more time you would need? I think your estimate was two hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I gave an estimate of three hours, and I believe that I will stick to the estimate.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, when I misspoke, I apologise for that. If your estimate was three hours in view of the material covered by this expert report, you can use your full three hours. We'll take a break, and we'll resume at 20 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Mladic. Mr. Mladic, no speaking aloud.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, if you are ready, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And I would like to thank Their Honours for the digression a moment ago, because those were precisely the issues I wanted to put questions about to Ms. Hanson.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If you remember, miss, one of -- one issue had to do with what was possible with the Crisis Staffs in terms of law and, quite apart from that, there were cases where you came across instances that Crisis Staffs issued orders, and you talked about it to Their Honours. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: What's more, as I read your report, I saw that you mentioned a number of cases, including Bosanska Krupa, and the Crisis Staff there. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: If my understanding is correct, in your CV, among other things, you stated that you testified in the case against Klickovic --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter isn't sure about the name.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: -- before the State Court of Bosnia-Herzegovina; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the case of Gojko Klickovic, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: He was the president of the Crisis Staff of Bosanska Krupa at the time. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned the case where he, as the president of the Crisis Staff and on behalf of the Crisis Staff, issued orders to the 1st Krajina Brigade on the 24th of April, 1992, about the use of that military unit which had to do with the destruction of certain bridges. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I would take the liberty to draw a conclusion, and I expect your reaction to it. The relationship between the army and the Crisis Staffs was defined in law, and that's true, but it's also true that, at the time in 1992, and especially in March, April, and May of 1992, based on the authority of the person heading the Crisis Staff and based on the authority of the senior officer who headed the JNA unit present in the area, it depended whether a JNA unit would, in fact, be used by Crisis Staffs. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's absolutely correct, except for the first part of your statement. I wouldn't say that the relationship between the army and the Crisis Staff was defined in law before May of 1992 but absolutely the second half, yes. One of the factors would be the authority of the person heading the Crisis Staff, and the authority of the personality of senior officer of the JNA. That's made clear in Karadzic's own words, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Another issue that I'd like to ask you about is this: I put it to you that, in terms of law, the composition of the Crisis Staffs did not include the senior officers of the JNA at local level. Am I right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: What law are you referring to when you say "in terms of law"? The problem is at what period of time are you talking about and what laws apply.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let me be more specific. In the period between December 1991 and end of May 1992, when the Crisis Staffs formally ceased to exist -- they were formed and formally ceased to exist, the compositions of the Crisis Staffs did not include the JNA senior officers present at that level; is that right?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: In some places they did. Zvornik, for example, names -- names the JNA commanders already when they form the Crisis Staff, and in his -- at assembly speech in March 1992, Krajisnik says, Form Crisis Staffs with JNA officers if you can. So I think the expectation would be, if possible, include them.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Let us now look at the instructions again together dated 19 December 1991. For the transcript, 65 ter number is 28386. Let's focus on part 2 of Variant A, first degree, item 3, which reads that the Crisis Staff shall be formed from, and then it lists members of the SDS Municipal Board secretariat members. Can you follow me? Then the holders of municipal offices. That's to say, president of the assembly, or president of the Executive Board, chief of the public security station, or commander of the police station, commander or chief of the TO staff, secretary of the Municipal Secretariat of National Defence, or other member of the secretariat who is a member of the SDS; next, deputies in the Assembly of the Serbian People of BH and members of the Main Board of the SDS from the area of the municipality concerned. Can you see here that no commanders of JNA units are mentioned here as members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I agree in this document from December 1991 it's not mentioned.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The Zvornik Crisis Staff is mentioned as an exception where the commander of the JNA -- of a JNA unit was appointed into the Crisis Staff. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I note also the Novo Sarajevo Crisis Staff invited battalion commanders to the Crisis Staff meetings. So those are the two places where I find it explicated before Karadzic's speech in March 27th. That's where I find specific references, the only two places.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to establish this further, let's look at 65 ter document 28387. They are conclusions from the meeting of the SDS Municipal Board in Zvornik held on the 22nd of December, 1991. In other words, three days after the issuance of the instructions. The agenda of which includes the election of the Crisis Staff. Do you see that, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The names of persons who are members of the Crisis Staff are listed here. The last line reads: "The Command Staff of the JNA of the municipality of Zvornik." Is that the document based on which you concluded that it was one of the exceptions to the instructions where a JNA commander was included in the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is the document I cite to in footnote 109.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Do you have any other document which would show that the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Zvornik included an officer of a JNA unit?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have very few documents of Zvornik before April 1992, so, no. And I specify in my text that they list the Command Staff as members, but assert that I have evidence that they were actively participating in Crisis Staff meetings before we see Crisis Staff -- a few Crisis Staff documents in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Since I am not concerned with the JNA but, rather, with the Army of Republika Srpska, my question will be placed in the context of the indictment. Did you find in any document evidence of the fact that any commander of the Army of Republika Srpska was a member of a Crisis Staff in the period up until Crisis Staffs ceased to exist in June of 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, not all Crisis Staffs ceased to exist in June 1992, and if you're limiting it to the commander of the VRS, we're limited to the period -- do you mean to limit to the ten-day period between the 21st of May and the 31st of May? Yes. The answer is yes. We talked about it in Sanski Most. Colonel Basara was a member of the Sanski Most Crisis Staff. Kljuc, we see that. Many, many Crisis Staffs, we see that. And through on into June. What I tend to see by July 1992 is not the commander himself but a deputy, a representative of the command, and that to me indicates the changing relationship. But in May and June, yes, I certainly see commanders of the regular army unit in the municipality on the Crisis Staffs.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You mentioned Sanski Most. And now I'm going to ask that we look at document 65 ter 06406.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, do you have any intention to -- to tender the conclusions of the Zvornik Municipal Board of the 22nd of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour, with all due respect, because I was basically forced to use this document. Thank you. May I proceed, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: These are conclusions from a meeting of the Crisis Staff held on the 21st and 22nd of April, 1992. The Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Sanski Most. Do you see that before you, Ms. Hanson?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Since you mentioned Sanski Most as one of the examples of a situation when an officer of the VRS was on the Crisis Staff, I'm going to ask you to look at paragraph 6 so that we comment on it. Again, I repeat, this is the 22nd of April, 1992. So this is what it says in paragraph 6: "The Crisis Staff of the Serbian municipality of Sanski Most hereby adopts the conclusion that the Serb defence forces are to be placed at the disposal of the commander of the Serb Territorial Defence and be engaged as a special unit of the Serb Territorial Defence." This is what I'm interested in now. To the best of your knowledge, in terms of the analysis of these documents, what kind of formations are these? Namely, the ones that the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most is referring to in April 1992?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it was a locally formed force, whether you want to call it volunteer, or paramilitary, or Serbian TO, there was a unit called the Serbian Defence Force, or SOS. But I note, as you said, this is April, so it's not relevant to the question of a VRS commander being on the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Then I'm going to ask you to look at 65 ter 06593. Let's take a look at it together. Also, this is a conclusion, or, rather, these are conclusions of the Crisis Staff of the Serb municipality of Sanski Most, but this is a month later, on the 22nd of May, 1992. In 1(d) of these conclusions, it says, in order to protect vital facilities of the town, above all the water supply system, the transformer station, the silo, et cetera, the commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade, Colonel Basara, and the commander of the Serbian Territorial Defence, Colonel Anicic, are hereby instructed to do that. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, do you draw the conclusion that Colonel Basara and Colonel Anicic are members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the basis of this alone, no. But I see other documents where they are listed. The Crisis Staff is assigning various tasks. Whether it is an order to an outside person or a tasking for a member of the Crisis Staff, it's hard to tell from this one sentence. But it is very common that the Crisis Staff in its conclusions assigns tasks to various people, and this one is assigning that to Colonel Basara and Anicic. But there are other documents in which Basara is listed.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to ask you a specific question now. Do you have a document that states that one of these two officers, as you say, of the Army of Republika Srpska was appointed member of the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most? Please take a look and do help us.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have an appointment but a listing of him as a leader -- as a member, yes, footnote 77, 65 ter 06408.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us what this document says, 06408.

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It lists the members --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could -- could we have a look at it. We have it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To my recollection, it lists the members and their various tasks. And Anicic is number 7 and Basara is number 10.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Please, let us take a look at this together. Let it be in accordance with the document that we have before us now. Mr. Anicic, at that point in time, that is to say, on the 30th of May, 1992, was he a member of the VRS; or, as is stated, commander of the STS?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: Is he listed here as a commander of the TO -- Serbian STO, presumably Serbian TO. As we know, this is the period of transition and the formation of the VRS. He is not listed here as a member of the VRS, per se.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now I'm going to ask that we go back to the document that was marked 06593. That's the 65 ter number. A moment ago, we looked at paragraph 1 (d) in that document, the conclusions of the 22nd of May, 1992. And then let us please look at paragraph 4. Same document. It says the following: "As far as disarming paramilitary formations in Sanski Most is concerned, as far as the practical side is concerned, Colonel Basara and Colonel Anicic are in charge." This is what I'm asking you now. This document and this conclusion, did you use this at any point in time as a basis to reach the conclusion that Anicic and Basara as members of the VRS are members of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: My conclusions are based on the totality of documents. When I had another one as of 30th of May listing him explicitly as a member of the Crisis Staff, and this is not in contradiction to it, I would -- I wouldn't say which document I based my conclusion on per se, but I cite -- obviously I cite to the other document. So this is not my sole source for such a statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I'm very sorry to interrupt you. May I put an additional question to the witness at this point in time. According to this document, we have seen on the screen, Colonel Basara was the commander of the 6th Krajina Brigade on the 30th of May. Can you tell me to which army did this brigade, the 6th Krajina Brigade, belong at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: At the 30th of May, to the VRS. According to the establishment of the VRS. The JNA no longer existed by that time was my understanding of it. The JNA ceased to exist effectively on the 27th of April, is my understanding, but the units were still there in place, and with the establishment of the VRS, unless they were withdrawing from Bosnia, they were part of the VRS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to finish on this note. If we agree that the commander of the unit from the VRS in Sanski Most was on the Crisis Staff on the 30th of May, 1992, would that be contrary to what the instructions of December 1991 say?

utterances.speaker: DOROTHEA HANSON [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would be very much in keeping with the spirit of the instructions. However, I regard the Variant A and B as being superceded by events by 30th of May, 1992. It would be in keeping with the instructions of 26 April 1992. It would be keeping -- in keeping with the instructions of 24 May 1992. But it is not explicated in December 1991 that the commander would be a member, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, we have to stop anyhow. But I have one question. There may be a translation issue, but I take it from your last question that you consider it - but correct me when I'm wrong - but it is your position that appointing a military commander would go against the instruction of the 19th of December. Is that your position? I see you're nodding yes, but ...

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour. Precisely. Because it is contrary --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, then we have to carefully look at the text of the -- it's my recollection, but I'm doing it from the top of my head, that the language, but there may be a translation issue, is that on the formation of the Crisis Staff that members should include. From what I remember, it doesn't say "the Crisis Staff are composed as follows" but that "the following persons should be included in the Crisis Staff." Which, of course -- I do not know if that is the issue you refer to, I'd like to know that, or whether there's any other portion where it apparently prohibits to have a member of the armed forces be appointed at the Crisis Staff, or were you referring to the -- to the part of the instructions I just referred to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With your leave, Your Honour, I'm going to respond and tomorrow when we continue, again, we are going to present paragraph A -- paragraph 3 of Variant A on the formation of Crisis Staffs to compare it to this. This is what our basic position is. As the distinguished witness said today, we have two Crisis Staffs where she found members of the VRS and those were exceptions. They were just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but the issue was a different one. The issue was whether it was inconsistent or it was contrary to the instructions to appoint a military commander on the Crisis Staff. That was the issue. Not on whether it was an exception or not. That's a different matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. We're going to show is that. Yes. We believe that it is contrary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. We'll then wait until tomorrow. Before we adjourn -- and perhaps -- Ms. Hanson, we'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 but then in Courtroom I again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: May I ask, if it's not rude, just to know how long to expect? It's just a question of my plans for later in the day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Stojanovic, if you stick to your three hours, then tomorrow you would have another 45 minutes approximately. So let's say that if we can assume that you finish in the first session, is that a correct expectation? Well, somewhere in --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- the end of the first session or early in the second session. Ms. Bibles, time for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think should be able to finish, based on what we have now, within the second session at the latest.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You -- you mean including possible ...

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Re-examination, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Re-examination for you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you take a full hour for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BIBLES
utterances.text: Assuming that cross may go into the end of the first session or even into the second session, then I should be able to finish within the second session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Which means that we'll certainly finish tomorrow. I would urge you to see whether we can -- re-examination of one hour is relatively long, but we'll finish tomorrow morning. But whether that will be at the end of the third session or at the end of the fourth session, which goes until 2.15, is unclear at this moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, we'd like to see you back but I'd first like to give you the same instructions that as I did yesterday not to communicate in any way with anyone about your testimony.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, you have not tendered anything yet. First, the instructions, would you like to have them in evidence? We may see them in the future many more times. And there are various versions of that one, I think, with and without handwritten notes on it, et cetera. Would you like to -- because this is one, yes, which is fully legible. Would you like to tender that?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. With your leave, I would like to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Registrar, 65 ter number 28386 would receive number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Number D78, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D78 is admitted into evidence. Any of the other documents you used?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter number 06593, conclusions of the Crisis Staff of the Serb Municipality of Sanski Most of the 22nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 06593 becomes Exhibit D79, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D79 is admitted into evidence. Any other documents?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I suggest - but otherwise we could call it as a Chamber exhibit - to have 06408 in evidence. I think I asked to look -- to be able to look at the document itself. If you -- I think you used it. If you do not want to tender it, then there are other ... I wrote ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just check whether I had the right number or was it 6406. Madam Registrar, could you assist us which one it was that we looked at.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I believe it was 06406, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, then I misheard. Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, it can also be our exhibit. And it is with pleasure that I will tender this as a Defence exhibit. The document of the Crisis Staff of Sanski Most, 06406.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Document 06406 becomes Exhibit D80, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: D80 is admitted into evidence. There may be one more, but we'll find out tomorrow. We'll not further stress the patience of those who are assisting us. As always, very loyal. We adjourn for the day, and we will resume tomorrow, the -- is it the -- yes.
